newsitem.title: USA: BASKETBALL-DILLARD LEAVES INDIANA STATE FOR JAMES MADISON JOB.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-DILLARD LEAVES INDIANA STATE FOR JAMES MADISON JOB.

text.p: Sherman Dillard, an All-America on the court at James Madison, quit as head basketball coach at Indiana State on Wednesday to take over the coaching reins at his alma mater.
Dillard departs Indiana State after three seasons and will replace Lefty Driesell, whose contract was not renewed for 1997-98.
The 41-year-old Dillard graduated magna cum laude from James Madison in 1978 after a basketball career in which he scored 2,065 points, second on the school's all-time list.
Indiana State was 4-24 the season prior to Dillard's arrival, and improved to 7-19, 10-17 and 12-16 in his tenure.

Before heading to Indiana State, Dillard was an assistant under Georgia Tech's Bobby Cremins from 1988-94, was on the staff of his college coach, Lou Campinelli, at California from 1985-88, and assisted Driesell at Maryland from 1979-85.
The 65-year-old Driesell had hoped to make the 1997-98 season his last one in an effort to record his 700th career collegiate victory. His contract expires on April 30.
The Dukes were 16-13 this season and finished second in the Colonial Athletic Association. They lost the conference final to Old Dominion, 62-58 in overtime.
